notes: Third full sweep (2026-10-22-b, head 0397dec): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call (each session used only Read on the input file, Write, Bash and, in opus-1, Edit), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. Expected reads (testing.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline.

Changed rule since db91c23, graded against the current text of references/testing.md: "Assert with patterns". Deciding sentence: "A value the test already holds goes into the pattern with the pin operator, `^subscriber`, or the whole value is compared with `==`; a match that binds the value and an `==` on it afterwards is the shape to replace." Count: 0 of 5 runs bind a value from the call under test and compare it with == afterwards; no elem/2, is_pid or length assertions this time. Judgment: opus-1 (lines 50-51), sonnet-1 (lines 57-58) and sonnet-2 (lines 49, 51) bind the pid returned by a start call and then assert Process.whereis(name) == pid. The value under test there is the whereis result, compared whole against a value the test holds, which the sentence allows, so these are graded clean; reading them as the forbidden shape would make opus and sonnet violated on this rule. The other graded rules are unchanged since db91c23 and are graded to the standard of the 2026-10-22 grade files. The SKILL.md changes (one-step with, the new do: rule, captures) are outside this case's list; I checked the outputs for them and found nothing to report.

"Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`" (unchanged since db91c23) is violated in 4 of 5 runs. start_link called from a test: opus-1 line 58, sonnet-1 lines 57 and 65, sonnet-2 lines 49 and 58; no run uses start_supervised/1 for the start-failure test. opus-1 also starts the server under the default global name in its async: true module (line 50), which the 2026-10-21 sweep graded violated for its opus-1. haiku-2 starts every server under the default name Notify.Subscriptions (line 21). Its module is async: false, but unlike the default-name tests the previous sweep excused, no test there is about the default, so it falls under "Give the process a test-specific name, or none" in the same way as the previous sweep's sonnet-1 with one fixed name for every test. haiku-1 is clean, with System.unique_integer names (line 22), which the previous sweeps graded clean. sonnet-2 starts its server through a hand-built child spec that calls GenServer.start_link without a name (lines 22, 26-33), which is under start_supervised!, so that part is not counted.

Judgment on "Use setup for shared data" (unchanged): sonnet-2's setup returns {:ok, server: server} (line 23), a keyword list rather than the map the rule names ("Return data from `setup` as a map"). ExUnit merges it into the context, and the tests match %{server: server} in their heads, so this is a strict reading. It is graded violated because the rule names the map form, and it is the first violation of this rule in any test-writing sweep. Reading the keyword form as allowed would make the sonnet tier clean. The other four runs return maps.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" is violated in 5 of 5: every run has describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" (opus-1 line 62, haiku-1 line 28, haiku-2 line 25, sonnet-1 line 69, sonnet-2 line 62). sonnet-1 also names tests only by their return value (line 70: test "subscribe returns :ok"; line 104: test "returns :ok"). Every run's describe "when a subscribed process exits" is a shared condition, which the rule allows. Previous sweep: 4 of 5.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 4 of 5 violate with async: false, forced by Process.register on the test pid (haiku-1 line 20, haiku-2 line 20, sonnet-2 line 21) or Application.put_env (sonnet-1 line 19). opus-1 is clean: async: true with a duplicate-keys Registry started in setup_all and keyed by the server pid, which the mailer double looks up with self() (lines 17, 26, 32). That is not the name key the rule shows, but it uses no global state, so it is graded clean as in the previous sweep. "Wait for messages, not for time": 3 of 5 violate with Process.sleep polling helpers (haiku-2 line 167, sonnet-1 line 49, sonnet-2 line 225; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 wait for :DOWN first and then still poll). opus-1 and haiku-1 wait for :DOWN and then make a synchronous call, and opus-1 also uses :sys.get_state before refute_received, so both are clean, an improvement on the previous sweep, where all five violated. Process.sleep(:infinity) in haiku-2 line 172 is the body that keeps a listener alive, and the single assert Process.alive?(server) checks (opus-1 line 191, haiku-2 line 141, sonnet-2 lines 191 and 202) are not polling, so neither is counted. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in all five.
Other rule outside the list: sonnet-2 line 22 pipes a single step ("Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom").

I ran the tests from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs, ten times each with random seeds. Every run passed every time with no compiler warnings (opus-1 15 tests, haiku-1 13, haiku-2 13, sonnet-1 20, sonnet-2 18). mix format --check-formatted passes on all five, which confirms format_ok in result.json.
